sources.claim: If an endorser has been paid or given something of value, that connection should be disclosed clearly; a platform's built-in disclosure tool is not automatically enough.

Fake or AI-generated reviews and testimonials that misrepresent real experiences are deceptive; the FTC has rules and guidance against fake reviews. The course teaches the principle (do not invent or buy reviews), not the rule's penalty details.

sections.skill: Use real reviews with permission and avoid fake ones

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: What should an owner do before quoting a customer on the website?

choices.text: Ask the customer for permission
Make up a name to protect privacy and add details
Quote them without asking, since the review is public
Change their words to sound more exciting

questions.correct_answer: Ask the customer for permission
questions.intro: Reviews and testimonials are powerful because they come from customers, so they must be REAL. Ask customers for permission before quoting them, use their actual words (fixing only small typos), and do not show a review as typical if it is not. Never write fake reviews, pay for positive reviews, or use AI to invent customer experiences; the FTC treats fake reviews and testimonials as deceptive. Respond calmly and helpfully to negative reviews; do not threaten or pay reviewers to remove them.
